item.title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.17570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Romanescu

item.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.17625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.
item.dc:creator: Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: The elephant random walk with proportionally growing recent memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.17664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study an elephant random walk with recent restricted memory, where at step $n$ the elephant remembers only the last $m_n=\max\{\lfloor cn\rfloor,1\}$ steps for $c\in(0,1)$. We show that the random walk undergoes a phase transition at the critical point $p_c=(3+\sqrt{1-c})/4$, which depends on the memory proportion $c$. For $0<p<p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n}$ is asymptotically normal; for $p=p_c$, $S_n/\sqrt{n\log n}$ is asymptotically normal; and for $p_c<p<1$, $S_n/n^{\rho}$ converges almost surely and in $L^2$ to a random variable for some constant $\rho\in (1/2, 1)$. This phase transition differs from that of the classical elephant random walk and its remote-memory counterpart, both of which have the same fixed critical point $3/4$.
item.dc:creator: Zhishui Hu, Shuwen Xue

item.title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $\phi^4_2$ fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.17716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.
item.dc:creator: Rubin Zhang, Ning Zhang

item.title: Domains of attraction of quasi-stationary distributions for an absorbed random walk
item.description: arXiv:2611.17791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a continuous-time random walk on the positive integers, killed at zero, where the downward rate $a$ and upward rate $b$ satisfy $a>b>0$. Its quasi-stationary distributions form a one-parameter family. We show that if the initial distribution $(m_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is strictly positive and satisfies $m_{n+1}/m_n\to r$, where $(b/a)^{1/2}<r<1$, then its conditional distribution given survival converges in total variation to the corresponding nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. We obtain asymptotic equivalents for the joint probabilities of position and survival, and for the survival probability itself. We also give a moment condition under which the minimal quasi-stationary distribution is selected. Finally, we construct an initial distribution whose successive-term ratios do not converge but whose conditional distribution nevertheless converges to a nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. Thus the ratio condition is sufficient but not necessary.
item.dc:creator: Phil. Pollett

item.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.
item.dc:creator: Maciej G{\l}uchowski, Georg Menz

item.title: The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.17911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<\beta<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{\beta^2}{4(1-\beta)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $\beta=1$, the rate changes to $\alpha_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $\beta_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Jalowy, Matthias L\"owe, Sara Terveer

item.title: Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.18353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cover times of uniform random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees, including the negative-parameter models corresponding to random $d$-ary increasing trees. We prove explicit limits in probability and expectation when the cover times are rescaled by $n (\log n)^2$. In particular, for the uniform random recursive tree the cover time is close to $e n (\log n)^2$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Omer Angel, Christina Goldschmidt, Peleg Michaeli

item.title: Squared Bessel particle systems with weak repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.18356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study squared Bessel particle systems with repulsion parameter $\kappa>0$ and dimension parameter $\delta\in\mathbb R$. We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $\delta$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<\kappa<1$ and do not occur for $\kappa\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<\kappa<1$.
item.dc:creator: Julia Lenczewska, Jacek Ma{\l}ecki, Szymon So{\l}tysiak

item.title: The roads taken in the directed landscape
item.description: arXiv:2611.18360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every finite-length path in the directed landscape spends almost all of its time on geodesics. More precisely, let G be the union of the interiors of all geodesics. We prove that, almost surely, every path of finite landscape length lies in G outside a set of times of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61. We also construct finite-length paths whose exceptional set has dimension at least 1/3. The proof combines quantitative bounds on nearly optimal detours, stochastic domination of the environment outside a geodesic, and a three-geodesic disjointness estimate.
item.dc:creator: Pranay Agarwal, Sourav Sarkar, B\'alint Vir\'ag

item.title: Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.18380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximation of the Smoluchowski coagulation equation by the Marcus--Lushnikov process with $N$ initial particles for the singular family of kernels $K\_\alpha(x,y)=x^{-\alpha}+y^{-\alpha}, \alpha > 0$. For regular mean-field particle systems, pathwise fluctuations are naturally expected on the scale $N^{-1/2}$, whereas sufficiently smooth observables may exhibit a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ after averaging. The singularity of $K\_\alpha$ at the origin makes it unclear whether this second-order mechanism survives. We prove that it does: for a class of sufficiently regular nonlinear functionals of the empirical measure, we establish a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ on finite time intervals. The main mechanism is a regularization produced by the singular dynamics itself. Small clusters coagulate at increasingly large rates, which generates exponential moments in the singular variable $x^{-\alpha}$ and yields a rapid escape from the singularity at zero. We exploit this phenomenon through a Wasserstein-type distance adapted to $x^{-\alpha}$, together with weighted total variation estimates used to construct and control the derivative of the Smoluchowski flow.
item.dc:creator: R{\'e}mi Catellier (UniCA, LJAD), Sebastian Baudelet-Aponte Garcia

item.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
item.description: arXiv:2611.18483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows. We then show that the equality phenomenon beyond the constant and linear sectors is already visible in the two-particle exclusion process. Such equality occurs in exactly two cases: either the harmonic $x$--$y$ voltage is $\frac12$ on every nonterminal vertex, and the induced nonterminal graph $G[V\setminus\{x,y\}]$ is disconnected; or the harmonic voltage is constant on each connected component of $G[V\setminus \{x,y\}]$, and both voltage values $a$ and $1-a$, with $0\le a<\frac12$, occur. In each case we compute the equality kernel in every degree and particle sector. The resulting decomposition gives the complete equality kernel for exclusion and, through the regular representation, for the interchange process.
item.dc:creator: Joe P. Chen

item.title: Internal diameter bounds for DLA on random planar maps under invariance principles
item.description: arXiv:2611.18540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sublinear bounds for the internal diameter of External Diffusion Limited Aggregation (DLA) clusters on random planar maps. We develop two conditional DLA growth results for deterministic planar maps: the weaker condition yielding sublinear growth for DLA, and the stronger yielding polynomially sublinear growth for DLA. We then verify the strong assumption a.s. for the $\gamma$-mated CRT maps, and the weak condition a.s. for ergodic scale-free random environments, establishing the corresponding a.s bounds.
item.dc:creator: Deven Mithal

item.title: Optimal Dividend Problem for a Threshold Dependent Surplus Process with Bounded Dividend Rate
item.description: arXiv:2611.17656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study optimal bounded-rate dividend payments for a diffusion surplus process whose drift and volatility change at a fixed surplus threshold. Optimal strategies admit an exhaustive classification into zero-threshold, positive single-threshold, two-boundary, and three-boundary configurations. The latter two configurations have separated dividend regions, which arise because the interface can reverse the monotonicity of the derivative of the value function with respect to the initial surplus. Multiband optimality requires an upward change in drift. Without prescribing a strategy in advance, we construct the unique bounded classical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman transmission problem by varying the derivative at zero surplus and selecting the unique value for which the resulting solution agrees in both value and derivative with a bounded solution at a fixed sufficiently large surplus level. Verification identifies this solution with the value function and determines the optimal feedback strategy. For each configuration, we derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and characterize the switching boundaries through explicit formulas or equations in one unknown obtained by matching the value function and its derivative. The analysis also shows how changes in the drift and volatility of the upper regime affect the optimal value and dividend strategy. Numerical analysis illustrates how model parameters affect the optimal dividend regions.
item.dc:creator: Zhongqin Gao, Panyu Wu, Xiaowen Zhou

item.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichm\"uller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.
item.dc:creator: Heiko Knospe, Jiahe Shen, Roger Van Peski

item.title: Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
item.description: arXiv:2611.17902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Chassagneux, St\'ephane Cr\'epey, Gr\'egoire Loeper, Justin Ruelland

item.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
item.description: arXiv:2611.17923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.
item.dc:creator: Miles E. Lopes, Ricardo Masini

item.title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
item.description: arXiv:2611.17934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.
item.dc:creator: Christian Bayer, Jakob Kellermann

item.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.17989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution. The analysis rests on a reduction: a vertex changes color, at most once, exactly when it is not a local maximum of a uniformly random labeling of the vertices, maxima being taken among the neighbors that share its initial color (the monochrome initial configuration is the slowest case). What can be predicted depends on what is known of the graph. The degree distribution (the view at distance one) gives the mean. The variance needs the view at distance two, in particular the triangles, and the full law needs the whole graph. We give closed-form results, from monochrome and from uniformly random initial configurations, on paths, cycles, random trees, Erd\H{o}s-R{\'e}nyi graphs and bipartite random graphs. From a monochrome start, the mean stays within a factor two of the worst case, whereas the variance ranges from zero (disjoint cliques) to order $n^2$ (the star on $n$ vertices)..
item.dc:creator: {\'E}lie de Panafieu (NPA), Fabien Mathieu (NPA), Maria Gradinariu Potop-Butucaru (NPA), S{\'e}bastien Tixeuil (NPA, IUF)

item.title: Real-Space-RG for the drawups and drawdowns of run-and-tumble trajectories: universality classes for models with space-dependent velocities and switching rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.18270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For one-dimensional run-and-tumble processes with the two velocities $v_{\pm}(x)$ and the two switching rates $\gamma_{\pm}(x)$, a given stochastic trajectory is an alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima corresponding to the switching events between the ballistic motions with velocities $v_{\pm}(x) $ in the two directions. The renormalized trajectory at scale $\Gamma$ is obtained by keeping only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $\Gamma$. Its statistical properties can be analyzed via the generalization of the previous work arxiv:2611.04853 concerning diffusion processes involving arbitrary diffusion coefficients $D(x)$ and Ito forces $F_I(x)$. The main result is that the scale function $s(x)$ of diffusion processes that depends only on the ratio $\frac{F_I(x)}{D(x) } $ is replaced by a pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ that depend only on the two ratios $\frac{\gamma_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{\gamma_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$. This pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ govern the exit probabilities from an interval and determine the universality classes of the renormalized trajectories: all run-and-tumble processes with the same two ratios $\frac{\gamma_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{\gamma_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$ share the same statistics of renormalized trajectories. This general framework is illustrated with examples that are compared to their diffusive counterparts : uniform symmetric and asymmetric processes on the whole line $x \in]-\infty,+\infty[$, geometric process on the half-line $x \in]0,+\infty[$, and an exponential functional of the telegraph process with a normalizable steady state.
item.dc:creator: Cecile Monthus

item.title: Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2611.18348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting the effects of multivariate dependence on the reliability of redundant systems.
item.dc:creator: Nuria Torrado

item.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
item.description: arXiv:2611.18373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $\Lambda_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.
item.dc:creator: Elena Agliari, Adriano Barra, Andrea Ladiana, Andrea Lepre, Diego Pallara

item.title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Antezana, Luciano Scazzola

item.title: Limitations of nonreversible lifts for subgeometric diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the effect of lifting on continuous-time Markov processes with potentially subgeometric convergence rates. Using a series of weak Poincar\'e-type inequalities, we derive a bound on the maximum acceleration that can be obtained through lifting. We present several examples to explore the sharpness of our derived bound, where the resulting bound has the same square-root order as in the spectral gap setting. Our results provide a framework for understanding the potential and limitations of non-reversible lifting beyond geometric convergence.
item.dc:creator: Mengxi Gao, Gareth O. Roberts, Andi Q. Wang

item.title: Convergence in Wasserstein Distance for Empirical Measures of Semilinear SPDEs
item.description: arXiv:2102.00361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The convergence rate in Wasserstein distance is estimated for the empirical measures of symmetric semilinear SPDEs. Unlike in the finite-dimensional case that the convergence is of algebraic order in time, in the present situation the convergence is of log order with a power given by eigenvalues of the underlying linear operator.
item.dc:creator: Feng-Yu Wang

item.title: The extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2202.01584v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motions. This is a particle system on the real line such that each particle has a type in addition to his position. Particles of type $1$ move on the real line according to Brownian motions and branch at rate $1$ into two children of type $1$. Furthermore, at rate $\alpha$, they give birth to children too of type $2$. Particles of type $2$ move according to standard Brownian motion and branch at rate $1$, but cannot give birth to descendants of type $1$. We obtain the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of particles of type $2$.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Ali Belloum

item.title: Heat kernel estimates for boundary traces of reflected diffusions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2312.08546v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the boundary trace processes of reflected diffusions on uniform domains. We obtain stable-like heat kernel estimates for such a boundary trace process when the diffusion on the underlying ambient space satisfies sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates. Our arguments rely on new results of independent interest such as sharp two-sided estimates and the volume doubling property of the harmonic measure, the existence of a continuous extension of the Na\"im kernel to the topological boundary, and the Doob--Na\"im formula identifying the Dirichlet form of the boundary trace process as the pure-jump Dirichlet form whose jump kernel with respect to the harmonic measure is exactly (the continuous extension of) the Na\"im kernel.
item.dc:creator: Naotaka Kajino, Mathav Murugan

item.title: Tilted Solid-On-Solid is liquid: scaling limit of SOS with a potential on a slope
item.description:
arXiv:2409.08745v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $(2+1)$D Solid-On-Solid (SOS) model famously exhibits a roughening transition: on an $N	imes N$ torus with the height at the origin rooted at $0$, the variance of $h(x)$, the height at $x$, is $O(1)$ at large inverse-temperature $ eta$, vs $\asymp \log |x|$ at small $ eta$ (as in the Gaussian free field (GFF)). The former--rigidity at large $ eta$--is known for a wide class of $|
abla\phi|^p$ models ($p=1$ being SOS) yet is believed to fail once the surface is on a slope (tilted boundary conditions). It is conjectured that the slope would destabilize the rigidity and induce the GFF-type behavior of the surface at small $ eta$. The only rigorous result on this is by Sheffield '05: for these models of integer height functions, if the slope $	heta$ is irrational, then Var$(h(x))	o\infty$ with $|x|$ (with no known quantitative bound). We study a family of SOS surfaces at a large enough fixed $ eta$, on an $N	imes N$ torus with a nonzero boundary condition slope $	heta$, perturbed by a potential $V$ on an $\epsilon_ eta$-fraction of sites (arbitrarily small). Our main result is (a) the measure on the height gradients $
abla h$ has a limit $\mu_\infty$ as $N	o\infty$; and (b) the scaling limit of a sample from $\mu_\infty$ converges to a full plane GFF. In particular, we recover the asymptotics Var$(h(x))\sim c\log|x|$. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a tilted $|
abla\phi|^p$ model, or a perturbation thereof, where the limit is recovered at large $ eta$. The proof looks at random monotone surfaces that approximate the SOS surface, and shows that (i) these form a weakly interacting dimer model, and (ii) the renormalization framework of Giuliani, Mastropietro and Toninelli '17 leads to the GFF limit. New ingredients are needed in both parts, including a nontrivial extension of [GMT17] from finite interactions to ones with exponential decay in the radius.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Laslier, Eyal Lubetzky

item.title: Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of the Athreya-Aldous-Shields Cascade and Related Mean Flow Equations
item.description: arXiv:2411.00629v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the discounted branching random walk process introduced by Athreya (1985) and Aldous and Shields (1988), referred to as the Athreya-Aldous-Shields (AAS) cascade. This process can be viewed as an idealized version of the stochastic model introduced by Le Jan and Sznitman in 1997 for the Navier-Stokes equations. The AAS cascade exhibits phase transitions at the critical branching rates $\alpha=1$ and $\alpha=2$. These transitions are reflected in the behavior of the associated mean flow equation, a nonlocal ODE referred to as the $\alpha$-Riccati equation. It is known that if $\alpha>1$, the AAS cascade is explosive in the sense of infinitely many splittings in finite time, and the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has at least two solutions. In this paper, we establish finer structural properties of an explosive AAS cascade and obtain a stronger non-uniqueness result. Namely, for each initial data in a certain range, the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has an infinite family of distinct solutions parametrized by their convergence rates at infinity. Our approach exploits a simple transformation between the AAS cascade and its "linearized" counterpart, whose mean flow equation is precisely the well-studied pantograph equation. This transformation demonstrates how a relationship at the level of stochastic processes can reveal an otherwise hidden relationship at the level of mean flow equations.
item.dc:creator: Radu Dascaliuc, Tuan N. Pham, Enrique Thomann, Edward C. Waymire

item.title: Triadic structures in multislice networks
item.description: arXiv:2504.00508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Networks provide a popular representation of complex data. Often, different types of relational measurements are taken on the same subjects. Such data can be represented as a multislice network, a collection of networks on the same set of nodes, with connections between nodes of different layers. For the analysis of multislice networks, we take inspiration from the analysis of simple networks, for which small subgraphs (motifs) have proven to be useful; motifs are even seen as building blocks of complex networks. A particular instance of a motif is a triangle, and while triangle counts are well understood for simple network models such as Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs, with i.i.d. distributed edges, even for simple multislice network models little is known about triangle counts. Here we address this issue by extending the analysis of triadic structures to multislice Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi networks. Again taking inspiration from the analysis of sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs, we show that the distribution of triangles across multiple layers in a multislice Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi network can be well approximated by an appropriate Poisson distribution. This theoretical result opens the door to statistical goodness of fit tests for multislice networks.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Ren, Tara Trauthwein, Gesine Reinert

item.title: Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations: exact exponents and scaling limits
item.description: arXiv:2510.26123v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study longest and shortest directed paths in the following natural model of directed random planar maps: the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation (UIBOT), which is the local limit of uniform bipolar-oriented triangulations around a typical edge. We construct the Busemann function which measures directed distance to $\infty$ along a natural interface in the UIBOT. We show that in the case of longest (resp.\ shortest) directed paths, this Busemann function converges in the scaling limit to a $2/3$-stable L\'evy process (resp.\ a $4/3$-stable L\'evy process). We also prove up-to-constants bounds for directed distances in finite bipolar-oriented triangulations sampled from a Boltzmann distribution, and for size-$n$ cells in the UIBOT. These bounds imply that in a typical subset of the UIBOT with $n$ edges, longest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/4}$ and shortest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/8}$. These results give the scaling dimensions for discretizations of the (hypothetical) $\sqrt{4/3}$-directed Liouville quantum gravity metrics. The main external input in our proof is the bijection of Kenyon-Miller-Sheffield-Wilson (2015). We do not use any continuum theory. We expect that our techniques can also be applied to prove similar results for directed distances in other random planar map models and for longest increasing subsequences in pattern-avoiding permutations.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Ewain Gwynne

item.title: Similarity-Sensitive Entropy under Representation Change and Inference
item.description: arXiv:2601.03064v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Similarity-sensitive entropy measures the uncertainty of a probability law relative to a similarity kernel that encodes the distinguishability of states. We develop the measure-theoretic treatment covering both finite similarity matrices and general probability spaces, and study how the law and similarity kernel transform under measurable maps, channels, and conditioning operations. This yields data-processing inequalities, so a reduction in entropy quantifies how much distinguishability is lost under representation change. We also define a conditional similarity-sensitive entropy theory, give a counterexample to a recent conjecture on concavity, and identify a practical one-dimensional Laplace kernel class where concavity holds.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Samuel Miller

item.title: Integrability properties and stochastic McKean-Vlasov dynamics with singular Lennard-Jones drift: a mesoscale regularization
item.description: arXiv:2601.22102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the convergence of the empirical measure of moderately interacting particle systems subject to singular forces derived by Lennard-Jones potential. Although the classical Lennard-Jones force is widely used in molecular dynamics, analytical results are not available. We consider a Lennard-Jones potential with free parameters in the McKean-Vlasov framework and proceed with a regularization at the mesoscale letting the particles interact moderately. We prove the well-posedness of the McKean-Vlasov SDE involving such singular kernels and the convergence of the empirical measure towards the solution of the McKean-Vlasov Fokker-Planck PDE, by means of a semigroup approach. We derive both the range of parameters characterizing the aggregation and repulsive force and the mesoscale order for which the convergence is achieved, by obtaining the right integrability regularity of the drift.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto M. Greco, Daniela Morale

item.title: Set-indexed and multiple sums in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.15783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider multiple and set-indexed sums of random vectors taking values in Euclidean space of growing dimension. It is shown that, when viewed as finite metric spaces, the sets of values of such sums converge in probability. The limit is identified as a generalization of the Wiener spiral, which appears as the high-dimensional limit of single-index sums.
item.dc:creator: Bochen Jin, Alexander Marynych, Ilya Molchanov

item.title: On Samuels' Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.18392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0\leq\mu_1\leq\cdots\leq\mu_n$ and let $\lambda>\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=\mu_i$, and write $D_i := \lambda-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}\mu_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<\lambda \right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{\mu_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Ling

item.title: Locally finite fixed points of branching Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2608.23202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a full characterization of the fixed points of Branching Brownian motion with critical and supercritical drifts under no additional assumptions besides it being locally finite almost surely. In particular, we do not assume finite intensity (Kabluchko, 2012) or the finite top particle (Chen-Garban-Shekhar, 2023) conditions. We also give a full characterization of the domain of attraction of the fixed points of BBM.
item.dc:creator: Xinxin Chen, Arnab Chowdhury, Atul Shekhar, Shuo Zhu

item.title: Well-posedness for Wright--Fisher SPDEs with measurable drift
item.description: arXiv:2609.23518v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove weak existence and uniqueness in law of $[0,1]$-valued solutions for a class of scalar stochastic heat equations with measurable drifts $b : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, driven by Wright--Fisher noise. The only assumptions we require on the drift are Borel-measurability, and the one-way inequalities $-Cu\leq b(u)\leq C(1-u)$ for some $C<\infty$, compatible with the necessary condition $b(1)\leq 0\leq b(0)$. These are vastly more general conditions than were previously available. Our proof relies on a stochastic duality between the solution of the stochastic heat equation, and a voting scheme running along the graph of a branching-coalescing particle system, generalising the class of drifts for which a dual process is available. Our results and their proof put the regularisation-by-noise result of Barnes, Mytnik and Sun, and its explanation, on a much more general footing.
item.dc:creator: Jere Koskela, Oliver Tough

item.title: Polynomial Decay in Absorbing Continuous-Time Markov Chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.27335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P(t)$ be the transition function of an absorbing continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space. We study asymptotic relations of the form $p_{ij}(t)\sim a_{ij} L(t)$, $t\to\infty$, where $L$ is independent of $i$ and $j$. We obtain general conditions under which the coefficient matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ has rank one and describe the resulting consequences for survival probabilities and conditional distributions. The analysis applies to both reducible and irreducible chains. We also construct an irreducible counterexample, based on a killed random walk on a homogeneous tree, for which a common asymptotic scale exists but the coefficient matrix has rank greater than one. This shows that irreducibility alone does not imply rank-one asymptotics. The results identify conditions under which fixed-state transition asymptotics determine the asymptotic behaviour of the entire transition function and clarify the limitations of such conclusions in the absence of additional structure.
item.dc:creator: Phil Pollett

item.title: Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fr\'echet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fr\'echet Means
item.description: arXiv:2610.28301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the Fr\'echet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity or semiconvexity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity of the population Fr\'echet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for its gradient at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On complete connected Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+\eta)$-moment, and local $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fr\'echet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fr\'echet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fr\'echet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. A flat-torus example exhibits anisotropic scaling, and two examples on the circle illustrate logarithmic smeariness and the failure of any deterministic linear scaling to yield a nondegenerate limit, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Yutaro Nakabayashi

item.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the localized regime $np^{\Delta/2}\gg(\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p\ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices in $H$, and identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this rare event. The degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ changes the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi picture in two ways. First, the hub construction that competes with a clique in the regime $p \gg n^{-1/\Delta}$ is not feasible here. Consequently, for $\Delta \geq 3$ throughout the entire localized regime, both the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by a planted almost-clique, of size roughly $\delta^{1/v_H}np^{\Delta/2}$. Second, as no clique in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ can be of size greater than $(d+1)$, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by $\lfloor\delta\rfloor$ many planted almost-cliques of size roughly $d$ and another planted almost-clique of size roughly $\{\delta\}^{1/v_H}d$. For cycles of even length, in lieu of pairs of almost-cliques each of size roughly $d$, the conditional structure may possess copies of almost-bicliques with each side roughly of size $d$. In the complementary regime $1\ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H}\ll(\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges and $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including regular $H$), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Basak, Shaibal Karmakar

item.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
item.description: arXiv:2611.13533v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Zhekai Pang

item.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
item.description: arXiv:2611.14576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Fluctuations in the non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma model with hierarchical interactions
item.description: arXiv:2408.08136v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a class of non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma models on a hierarchical lattice. We prove that the hyperbolic distance between the superspin at any vertex and a reference superspin has asymptotically small fluctuations for large enough interactions, uniformly in the size of the graph and in the choice of the vertex. This can be viewed as a spontaneous breaking of the Lorentz boost symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Margherita Disertori, Franz Merkl, Silke W. W. Rolles

item.title: Extensibility and denseness of periodic monoid actions
item.description: arXiv:2502.00312v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A monoid has the periodic approximation (PA) property if, for every full shift on a finite alphabet, finitely supported invariant probability measures are weak-* dense in the space of invariant Borel probability measures. We introduce the class of measure-theoretically extension-compatible (MEC) monoids, consisting of embeddable monoids for which every probability measure-preserving (p.m.p.) action admits an invertible p.m.p. extension. For an embeddable monoid $S$ with free $S$-group $(\Gamma,\gamma)$, we prove that the PA property implies MEC, and that the converse holds whenever $\Gamma$ has the PA property. We establish that every left reversible bicancellative monoid and every finitely generated free monoid is MEC, and deduce the PA property for left amenable monoids that are residually a finite group and for finitely generated free monoids. Moreover, for $S=\mathbb F_d^+$, we characterize the free $S$-group as the unique receiving $S$-group for which all fully supported invariant Markov measures on full shifts on finite alphabets admit invariant invertible extensions.
item.dc:creator: Raimundo Brice\~no, \'Alvaro Bustos-Gajardo, Miguel Donoso-Echenique

item.title: Multi-period Asset-liability Management with Reinforcement Learning in a Regime-Switching Market
item.description: arXiv:2509.03251v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper explores the mean-variance portfolio selection problem in a multi-period financial market characterized by regime-switching dynamics and uncontrollable liabilities. To address the uncertainty in the decision-making process within the financial market, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. Specifically, the study examines an exploratory mean-variance (EMV) framework where investors aim to minimize risk while maximizing returns under incomplete market information, influenced by shifting economic regimes. The market model includes risk-free and risky assets, with liability dynamics driven by a Markov regime-switching process. To align with real-world scenarios where financial decisions are made over discrete time periods, we adopt a multi-period dynamic model. We present an optimal portfolio strategy derived using RL techniques that adapt to these market conditions. The proposed solution addresses the inherent time inconsistency in classical mean-variance models by integrating a pre-committed strategy formulation. Furthermore, we incorporate partial market observability, employing stochastic filtering techniques to estimate unobservable market states. Numerical simulations and empirical tests on real financial data demonstrate that our method achieves superior returns, lower risk, and faster convergence compared to traditional models. These findings highlight the robustness and adaptability of our RL-based solution in dynamic and complex financial environments.
item.dc:creator: Zhongqin Gao, Ping Chen, Xun Li, Yan Lv, Wenhao Zhang

item.title: Multipole and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transitions in the Two-component Plasma
item.description: arXiv:2509.09449v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the two-dimensional two-component Coulomb gas in the canonical ensemble and at inverse temperature $\beta>2$. In this regime, the partition function diverges and the interaction needs to be cut off at a length scale $\lambda\in (0,1)$. Particles of opposite charges tend to pair into dipoles of length scale comparable to $\lambda$, which themselves can aggregate into multipoles. Despite the slow decay of dipole--dipole interactions, we construct a convergent cluster expansion around a hierarchical reference model that retains only intra-multipole interactions. This yields a large-deviation result for the number of $2p$-poles as well as a \textcolor{black}{free-energy expansion} as $N\to\infty$ and $\lambda\to0$, with three contributions: (i) the free energy of $N$ independent dipoles, (ii) a perturbative correction, and (iii) the contribution of a non-dilute subsystem. The perturbative term has two equivalent characterizations: (a) a convergent Mayer series built from non-divergent elementary dipole activities; and (b) a variational formula as the minimum of a large-deviation rate function for the empirical counts of $2p$-poles. The Mayer coefficients \textcolor{black}{should undergo} transitions at $\beta_p=4-\tfrac{2}{p}$\textcolor{black}{, and these thresholds} accumulate at $\beta=4$, which corresponds to the \textcolor{black}{Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless} transition in the low-dipole-density limit. \textcolor{black}{We prove that the limiting $p$-dipole activities are finite for $\beta>\beta_p$.} The non-dilute system corresponds to the contribution of large dipoles. For $2<\beta<4$, the independent-dipole dilution estimate predicts the critical length scale $R_{\beta,\lambda}=\lambda^{-(\beta-2)/(4-\beta)}$. For $\beta\geq4$, we set $R_{\beta,\lambda}=+\infty$, as this estimate gives no algebraic crossover scale in $\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Jeanne Boursier, Sylvia Serfaty

item.title: General coupling-based f-divergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2510.07559v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A long-standing gap exists between the theoretical analysis of Markov chain Monte Carlo convergence, which is often based on statistical divergences, and the diagnostics used in practice. We introduce the first general convergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo based on a broad class of f-divergence, allowing users to directly monitor, among others, the Kullback-Leibler and the chi-squared divergences as well as the total variation distance. Our approach rests on a coupling-based 'weight harmonization' scheme that produces direct, computable, and consistent importance weights for interacting Markov chains with respect to their target distribution. Beyond their use as convergence diagnostics, these weights give unbiased estimates of the Radon-Nikodym derivative between the un-normalized target and the distribution of the current iterate, a richer object than the convergence bounds alone, with natural applications to importance-weighted inference. We show how such weightings can provide asymptotic upper bounds to any f-divergence, prove that these bounds converge to zero as the chains approach stationarity, and demonstrate that, while more conservative than existing coupling-based total variation estimators, our method remains a practical and broadly applicable diagnostic tool.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Corenflos, Hai-Dang Dau

item.title: Central Limit Theorems for Common Zeros via Bergman Kernels
item.description:
arXiv:2603.04588v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove central limit theorems as \(N	o\infty\) for common-zero statistics of \(k\) independent standard Gaussian holomorphic sections of \(L^N\), where \(L\) is a positive Hermitian holomorphic line bundle over a compact K"ahler manifold of complex dimension \(m\). For fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) forms \(\varphi\) of bidegree \((m-k,m-k)\) with \(\partial ar\partial\varphi
ot\equiv0\), we prove the CLT in codimensions \(2\leqslant k\leqslant m\) and show that the integrated coefficient in the Shiffman--Zelditch variance formula at scale \(N^{2k-m-2}\) is strictly positive. Shiffman and Zelditch proved the unconditioned smooth CLT for \(k=1\). For \(1\leqslant k\leqslant m\) we also prove a CLT for weighted volumes in fixed domains \(U\) with \(\mathscr C^2\) boundary and fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) weights \(f\) whose restriction to \(\partial U\) is not identically zero. The variance of a weighted volume is asymptotic to \(N^{2k-m-1/2}
u_{m,k}\int_{\partial U}f^2\,\mathrm d\sigma\), with \(
u_{m,k}>0\) the Shiffman--Zelditch boundary constant and \(\sigma\) the induced surface measure. For \(k=m\) and \(f\equiv1\), the statistic counts common zeros in \(U\). Conditioning each section to vanish on the same fixed finite set preserves the leading variance and the Gaussian limit for both classes of tests, including smooth tests for \(k=1\). The set may meet \(\partial U\). A Bergman kernel criterion yields variance bounds and the new unconditioned CLTs from a uniform local \(L^2\) Bargmann--Fock limit and integrable off-diagonal derivative bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bin Guo

item.title: The SK model with a sparse variance profile: free energy and AMP-based magnetization estimation at high temperature
item.description: arXiv:2604.25535v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A generalization of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model for spin glasses is considered, in which the interaction matrix is endowed with a variance profile that has no particular structure and may be sparse. In the first part of the paper, an asymptotic equivalent of the free energy is derived at sufficiently high temperatures, regardless of the signature of the variance profile matrix. In the second part, the mean of the spin vector under the Gibbs measure is estimated using an Approximate Message Passing algorithm that generalizes the one used for the SK case. The dynamical approach of Adhikari et al (J Stat Phys 2021), originally developed for the classical SK model, is adapted to the present setting to obtain these results.
item.dc:creator: Walid Hachem

item.title: Non-monotone clustering and energetic regime switching in aggregation-diffusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.30243v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate transient clustering dynamics in nonlocal aggregation-diffusion systems from an energetic perspective. Starting from a stochastic interacting particle system, we study the associated macroscopic McKean-Vlasov equation on the torus and use its Wasserstein gradient-flow structure to analyse the competition between interaction-driven aggregation and entropy-driven diffusion. Through numerical experiments for locally attractive interaction kernels, we observe non-monotone clustering behaviour in intuitive geometric observables: in particular, the density peak height may first increase and subsequently decrease along trajectories converging to equilibrium. Using the decomposition of the free energy as a diagnostic, we identify alternating aggregation- and diffusion-dominated regimes underlying these transient dynamics. We investigate to what extent transitions between these regimes are related to the evolution of geometric observables, such as the peak height. Our results illustrate how non-monotone transient clustering can arise even in a dissipative gradient-flow system and highlight the complementary information provided by geometric clustering observables and the free-energy-based regime classification.
item.dc:creator: Nathalie Wehlitz, Richard Scherzer, Carsten Hartmann, Stefanie Winkelmann

item.title: Kinetic Fokker-Planck Equations with Nonlinear Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2607.00458v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study existence, regularity, and uniqueness for the nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equation $$ \partial_t f=\Delta_v\Psi(f)-v\cdot\nabla_x f, \qquad f|_{t=0}=f_0, $$ on $\mathbb R^{2d}$. In the model case $\Psi(r)=r^s$, this equation couples nonlinear fast-diffusion/porous-medium type diffusion with kinetic transport. A distinctive feature is that the diffusion acts only in the velocity variable $v$, so that compactness in the spatial variable $x$ cannot be obtained from standard elliptic estimates and must instead be recovered through the hypoelliptic structure. Under general structural assumptions on $\Psi$, including the fast-diffusion powers $\Psi(r)=r^s$ with $s\in(0,1)$, we construct nonnegative weak solutions and prove quantitative anisotropic Besov regularity estimates. Under an additional mass-critical growth condition on the fast-diffusion side, the constructed weak solution preserves mass, admits a renormalized kinetic formulation, and is unique in the $L^1$-class of mass-preserving renormalized kinetic solutions. In the power-law case $\Psi(r)=r^s$, this condition is precisely $s\ge 1-1/d$ when $d\ge2$, while in dimension $d=1$ the whole fast-diffusion range $s\in(0,1)$ is covered. The main analytic ingredient is a parameter-dependent smoothing estimate for the kinetic semigroup generated by $$ \Psi'(\zeta)\Delta_v - v\cdot\nabla_x , $$ which quantitatively tracks the dependence on the kinetic level $\zeta$. Combined with the kinetic formulation, this estimate yields compactness in both spatial and velocity variables for the nonlinear hypoelliptic problem. As an application, we also obtain martingale-problem solutions to the associated distributional-density dependent stochastic differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Zimo Hao, Zhengyan Wu, Xicheng Zhang

item.title: Optimal MM* bounds for convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2607.29458v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K\subset\R^n$ be a convex body in isotropic position. We prove the optimal mean-width estimate \[ M^*(K)\leq C\sqrt{n\log n}. \] The main new ingredient is a geometric inequality relating the Gaussian mean of the support function to its mean under the uniform measure on $K$, obtained through a heat-flow argument. Combined with the Gaussian-log-concave comparison of Eldan and Lehec and the newly available dimension-free bound on the third-moment parameter $\kappa_n$, this yields the result. The boundedness of $\kappa_n$ also makes the mean-norm estimate of Bizeul and Klartag sharp. Combining both estimates yields \[ M(K)M^*(K)\leq C\log n, \] extending Pisier's $MM^*$ estimate to non-symmetric convex bodies and to the isotropic position.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bizeul

item.title: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30106v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $\theta = \Pr(N=1) \in (0, \theta_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $\theta$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.
item.dc:creator: Jordi Valero, Josep Ginebra

item.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06041v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
item.description: arXiv:2611.12258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Garbali, Cengiz Gazi, Jan de Gier, William Mead, Michael Wheeler
